probes.timeoutJustification: This probe cannot complete inside the attach window and trimming it to fit would silently drop the reading it exists for. It needs a LIVE FRAME LOOP, because everything it measures is produced by CClock::HeartbeatBefore and there are no heartbeats before the engine is running frames -- and it needs the stage-0 tick source, which is W1-D's CNSProvider slot claim and does not go live until the provider slots are populated (W1-D gives that its own 120 s deadline). After the tick starts the measurement itself is about 950 frames, which is 16 s at 60 Hz and 11 s at 90 Hz: 1 frame for the at-rest census, 30 to let the clock take and settle, 16 consecutive paused samples, 4 for one armed frame-step, 600 for the five rate cells, 300 to re-read the floor far enough after we wrote it to mean something, and 2 to release and confirm the restore. 300 s is 120 s of slot-claim deadline plus that measurement plus margin for a slower boot; the worker's own deadline is 270 s so the verdict is WRITTEN before the harness kills the process rather than lost with it. The 300-frame late-floor wait is the one number that could be trimmed, and it is the one that must not be: the whole point of the pair is that it is far enough apart to catch a writer.
probes.why: COLLECTS ALL SEVEN of W2-D's parked reads, and the one that matters is clock-paused-scaled-delta, the read half of DL-05. A stock CClock leaves CLOCK.MINELAPSED_OFF at ZERO -- sub_1400CD8F0 sets it and an image-wide sweep of stores to +0x58 finds no other writer -- and with a zero minimum the engine's OWN pause bit is a live divide by zero: paused gives raw 0 at 0x1400CF406, clamp(0,0,66666) is 0 both before and after the multiply, so CLOCK.SCALEDDELTA_OFF is 0, CLOCK.UNNAMED_3C_OFF is 0.0f, and the divss at 0x1400CF6FB puts 1.0f/0.0f = +inf into CLOCK.RECIP_OFF and from there into every consumer of the frame reciprocal. src/engine/clock.cpp therefore writes a 1 us floor BEFORE it ever sets the pause bit and REFUSES to pause if the floor does not read back (ClockRefusal::NoFloor). Nothing has ever confirmed any of that in a running engine. This probe pauses through the shipping IReplayClock and asserts over 16 consecutive frames that CLOCK.SCALEDDELTA_OFF is never 0 and CLOCK.RECIP_OFF is never 0x7F800000. IT CANNOT PASS VACUOUSLY: a finite reciprocal on an unpaused clock is what an untouched engine produces all day, so every sample also records CLOCK.FLAGS_OFF and the check is UNDETERMINED unless bit 1 was observed SET on every scored sample -- the discriminating question is not whether the reciprocal is finite but whether it is finite WHILE THE PAUSE BIT IS SET. The red arm is deliberately NOT constructed in vivo: making this check fail on demand means writing 0 back into +0x58 and pausing, which injects +inf into a running physics engine on the owner's machine, and it is refused; the arithmetic's red arm is compiled and run offline in tests/clock (both mutants take that gate red, 54 assertions, checked=0). THE AT-REST CENSUS RUNS FROM A MODULE AT ORDER 305, one before the clock module at 310, because modreg ticks modules in ascending order within one stage-0 tick -- so on the very first tick this module reads the three clocks exactly as the engine left them, before anything of ours has been written. Reading them from a worker thread would race the first Apply and could not say which side of it a sample came from, which is the difference between a census of the engine and a census of ourselves. It dereferences CLOCK.GLOBAL_PTR, CLOCK.THIRD_PTR and CR15Game+GAME_CLOCK_PTR_OFF, and for each reports the pointer, its vtable, and vtable slot +8 -- which must be TICK.HEARTBEAT_BEFORE, because that is the function whose clamp order every offset in this module was derived from. That check matters most for CLOCK.THIRD_PTR, which the registry knows only as an address SetMaxElapsedUS stores +0x60 to; its layout at +0x38 and +0x50 is an inference from a single field, and this turns the inference into an observation or refuses the clock. It also reports +0x78, the RAW microseconds of the last heartbeat, which no fact registers and which would give the frame period independently of QueryPerformanceCounter. NO TRANSPORT IS LINKED and done.json says so in its own note: ReplayServices::transport is null, the clock's mirror is inert, and the probe drives IReplayClock through its public API -- which is what lets ONE launch answer the rate and step reads without a demo file. The register state under test is identical either way, since pause is CLOCK.FLAGS_OFF bit 1 whoever asked for it, but this run does NOT establish that IReplayTransport::Pause() reaches the clock and does not claim to. EXCLUSIVE because this probe WRITES the engine clock: it pauses the world, drives the timescale to 0.1x and 4.0x, and installs a floor. Any other probe in the same launch would be measuring a world we slowed down, and would have no way to know. It also RELEASES at the end and reports CLOCK.FLAGS_OFF afterwards, so a launch that continues does not inherit a clock nobody configured. GUARDS offline-bit-lock, and the declaration is backed by a mechanism: DllMain calls replay::bootstrap::Attach, which is what installs the lock -- linking replay_bootstrap puts the code in the binary without ever running it -- and WriteVerdict then reads offlinelock::Current().state out of shared memory, so it reports what the hook observed for the PROCESS rather than whether this module won the install race, and FAILS the run when the process is not protected. AlreadyLockedInProcess is scored as held, because every probe DLL links the library and MinHook refuses the duplicate installs.
probes.scope: ESTABLISHES, if it returns PASS: that with CLOCK.FLAGS_OFF bit 1 observed SET, CLOCK.SCALEDDELTA_OFF is never 0 and CLOCK.RECIP_OFF is never +inf on the global clock -- with CLOCK.FLAGS_OFF bit 1 set BY THIS PROBE through IReplayClock -- the engine does not set it -- the engine's own per-frame update produces neither a zero scaled delta nor an infinite reciprocal, which is DL-05's read half for a clock WE paused, which is DL-05's read half; that the object at CLOCK.GLOBAL_PTR is stepped by TICK.HEARTBEAT_BEFORE, so the clamp order every offset was derived from applies to it; and that the floor we wrote was still present hundreds of frames later, which is the only way to establish that nothing else writes CLOCK.MINELAPSED_OFF -- the offline sweep is keyed on the [reg+58h] displacement and is structurally blind to a writer that computes the field address into a register first. DOES NOT ESTABLISH that IReplayTransport::Pause() reaches the clock: no transport is linked, the mirror is inert, and the probe drives IReplayClock directly. DOES NOT ESTABLISH that the fast-forward ceiling is 4.0x or 6.0x on any other display: the rate cells report the frame period they were measured at, and above the ceiling the CORRECT achieved rate is the ceiling, not the commanded rate, so a 4.0x command reading back as 4.0x at 60 Hz is the ceiling and the rate agreeing and is not a discriminating cell. DOES NOT ESTABLISH the absence of a +0x58 writer as an image-wide claim -- it establishes that none fired in this run, over the frames sampled. A COULD-NOT-DETERMINE means the tick source never went live, the global clock was never constructed, or the build is not the measured echovr.exe; none of those is a defect report. A FAIL on offline-bit-lock-held means the process was NOT protected and the launch should be treated as unprotected whatever any descriptor declared. A FAIL on paused-delta-never-zero is the serious one: it means the floor did not take and every consumer of CLOCK.RECIP_OFF received +inf while this probe was paused.
